summary: A voter grades a leader by prices at the store, holds him to a promise to cut them, and still votes the same way.
realLife: Swing voters from a big state talk about politics through small purchases: the dollar store that crept up, groceries, gas and milk. One calls the grade a C after a B-plus, another a D, one a D-minus because she cannot give an F. They hold the leader to his promise on prices and blame tariffs and a war. Two say they would vote the same way again given the choices.
sources: https://www.michiganpublic.org/2026-09-03/pennsylvania-swing-voters-say-trump-hasnt-delivered-on-promise-to-lower-prices (NPR Swing Shift interviews, via a member station)
gates: the speaker has voted for both parties
the speaker buys groceries and gas for a household
the candidate won on a promise about prices
weights: how much of the household's pay food takes
whether the speaker follows the news
inGame: reads the speaker's prices paid against a promised effect on prices and the candidate's record; the vote is a stand with a reason

turns.what: She raises the grade after gas got cheaper.
turns.writesBack: her stand on the leader is re-graded with the cause

turns.what: He says it is a D and he would still vote the same.
turns.pulledBy: the other option is worse in his eyes
turns.writesBack: the vote record is unchanged beside a low grade

turns.what: She says she will not vote for him again.
turns.pulledBy: a broken promise plus his conduct
turns.writesBack: her party tie is cut; the vote record flips
